Hi Rachel — great to hear the demo was useful. Below is a concise recommendation that we can iterate on:

1) Pilot package (recommended):
- "Optimize Starter Pilot" — 1.75M token credits, 4 weeks, includes access to Optimize tooling (batching/caching advisor, quantization playbooks), and one architecture review with our inference team.
- One-off 25% pilot credit applied to the token pool (so you'd get 2.1875M tokens chargeable as 1.75M).

2) Commercial framing:
- If you convert to a 6-month committed band within 30 days after pilot close, we can apply a 15% committed discount on token consumption and a committed capacity uplift for predictable throughput.
- If procurement prefers usage-based (no commit), we recommend a capped monthly spend for first 2 months to limit exposure; we can model that in the attached estimate.

3) Quantization guidance (high level):
- Start with 8-bit integer (int8) quantization for the pilot — it's the lowest-risk path for production parity on most open LLMs we recommend.
- 4-bit can be considered for cost-sensitive paths but should be evaluated on a prompt-by-prompt basis: certain few-shot setups and instruction-following prompts can see a small accuracy delta.
- Our standard recommendation: int8 for mainline inference; evaluate key prompts for 4-bit only if the int8 economics don't meet your target. Karthik can confirm compatibility with your model family.

4) Measurement & observability: 
- We'll provide per-route dashboards: token consumption, token cost, P50/P95 latency, cache hit rates, and a small quality test harness you can run against target prompt sets.
- Suggested evaluation metrics: BLEU/ROUGE is rarely useful for instruction models — we recommend a small human-eval set (10–30 prompts) and automated pass/fail checks for safety/regression.

Attachments: fincube_pilot_estimate.xlsx (pilot cost scenarios), optimize_package_summary.pdf (package inclusions).

Next steps: If that sounds OK, I can loop in our billing/ops contact for an initial SOW sketch and a pilot invoice.

Quick tech confirm:
- Int8 is our recommended default for the Llama-variant you mentioned (20B). Expect <2% quality delta on typical instruction prompts in our internal benchmarks; however, some few-shot contexts with many exemplars can be more sensitive.
- KV cache: long-context use cases (3k+ tokens) will benefit from prefix KV caching — we can enable prefix caching at the route level during the pilot to reduce repeated compute. Cache hit rates will be reported in the dashboard.
- 4-bit paths: we can do a short A/B within the pilot to check 4-bit viability on your 10 highest-value prompts; we recommend running the 4-bit tests after an initial int8 baseline is established.

Happy to run the A/B and include results in the weekly checkpoint.
